constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; submit only submission/trojan_report.json.
The netlist inputs/key_core_netlist.v is provided as-is in structural Verilog (gate-level, using a small standard-cell-like library of DFF, MUX2, AND, OR, NOT primitives) and must not be edited.

Base your findings solely on static/behavioral analysis of the provided netlist and, optionally, simulation via yosys/iverilog/vvp against the provided scan_chain_order.txt; no other side-channel data is available.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing a trojan_detected boolean, a list of suspect flip-flop instance names, a list of suspect mux/gate instance names, and a free-text rationale

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON parseable by a standard JSON library and must contain all five required top-level fields (trojan_detected, suspect_flops, suspect_muxes, confidence, rationale) with the exact types specified in the interface.

suspect_flops and suspect_muxes must each be JSON arrays of strings; every string listed must correspond to an actual instance name found in inputs/key_core_netlist.v (no fabricated or misspelled instance names).
confidence must be a numeric value in the inclusive range [0.0, 1.0].
rationale must be a non-empty string of at least 20 characters describing the reasoning used to identify the listed flops and muxes.

interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (UTF-8, no trailing comments). Required top-level schema: { "trojan_detected": <boolean>, "suspect_flops": [<string>, ...], "suspect_muxes": [<string>, ...], "confidence": <number 0.0-1.0>, "rationale": <string> }. "suspect_flops" must list exact Verilog instance names of flip-flop cells from inputs/key_core_netlist.v that the participant judges to be scan-observable in a way inconsistent with normal isolated operation. "suspect_muxes" must list exact instance names of the multiplexer/gating cells the participant judges responsible for splicing those flops onto the scan path. evaluate.py reads inputs/key_core_netlist.v (and optionally invokes iverilog/vvp to simulate scan_en/scan_in/scan_out behavior against inputs/scan_chain_order.txt) purely for reference and cross-checking; it does not execute or modify the submission file. Field names, casing, and types above are exact and mandatory; unrecognized extra fields are ignored.
objective: Analyze the supplied gate-level netlist of a small crypto core with an embedded scan-test infrastructure. The design integrates a scan chain (ports scan_en, scan_in, scan_out) alongside a functional key register. Your task is to review the netlist and produce a structured analysis report identifying which flip-flops are reachable on the scan-out path during scan-mode capture-and-shift, and which specific mux instances establish that reachability, so that test engineers can assess whether test infrastructure inadvertently exposes internal state that should remain functionally isolated from the scan network.
response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
